subject: The one day I don't look at the forums!
author: ZombieTron
body:
What did I miss?? I had one quiet moment this afternoon at work where I looked on here and saw the Kev? blog, so I went to the CG forums to see what was going on.. but then my boss wanted me to move stations so I had to log off before I could see anything.. now I am home and the forums are gone??

Oh well, I was just saying to Xandu yesterday how extremely boring the CG forum had become over the last few anyway, so it really isn't a huge loss to the community IMO.

I think it would be nice for CG to put up a page explaining why they closed the forums and thanking us all for our contributions over the last however long the forums have been open, instead of just webpage not found. They have updated the webpage to remove the forum links, it's kind of like the forum never existed!

I'm sure Alex, and some other members of the Burnout Team may still lurk on the fansites, and we may even see them post again. 🙂

And to all those who comment about Burnout Team members personally and call them names.. Please don't.

Alex Ward and the rest of the team were all really lovely to us when we went to visit them, and although we may not agree with the direction the Burnout Series has taken in the last year, there is no need to insult people on a personal level. Please keep your criticism constructive!

It was fun having an official forum. It could of been run a lot better, but it's not easy to manage a forum that is as active as the official forum was.

Thank You to Criterion Games for providing us with an official forum, and for answering all (or most) of our questions, even the really silly ones! It was AWESOME to be able to have the kind of contact that the forum provided! 🙂

I'm sorry it had to end like this, and I hope you will learn from the experience of having an official forum and consider creating another one some time down the road.

subject: Rofer....
author: Jinno Angelo
body:
Just to let you know Rofer, the question I asked him was:

Seeing how No one goes into the Revenge forums anymore, Revenge fans cant post their opinions on how to make Revenge better, so In turn we go to the Paradise forums because it is the only place where our opinions can heard or answered. While our intention is not to start wars or flame people, it is to let our opinions be heard about how dissatisfied we are with Paradise. But although we are dissatisfied with Paradise, we are also keeping Burnout alive by playing these previous titles such as Revenge.

Now, although a minority of us do post about how we dont like Paradise, the majority of the people who complain about Paradise can be satisfied by creating one or two tracks for Revenge. If he says that he reads other forums, maybe even this one, and he knows what he want, how come he hasnt created one or two tracks to keep the Revenge players satisfied when we in turn already have suggested that we will buy credits and pay for it? Even long time players will probably pay for new tracks again. As a developer of the game, is he supposed to just let the Revenge players left out? Are we as Revenge players who are not satisfied with Paradise supposed to just let this one slide? After all, it is the hardcore players and the ones dedicated to the series that do stay with the games and keep them alive.... 

This question was answered by zerojay, and I gave thanks to zero for replying but I directed this question namely to the staff at Criterion... I didnt even get an answer back except a closed forum... As I said, it was not my intention to start a war, it was just a serious question that deserves a serious answer...

 

Now he can answer this and say that financially, it might not be the best idea for them... I would have accepted that, I wasnt flaming when I asked the question... But I got a closed forum as a response...

------------------------------------------
